question: A 31-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of low-grade intermittent fever, dyspnea, and chest pain that worsens on deep inspiration. Over the past 4 weeks, she has had pain in her wrists and the fingers of both hands. During this period, she has also had difficulties working on her computer due to limited range of motion in her fingers, which tends to be more severe in the morning. Her temperature is 37.7°C (99.8°F). Physical examination shows a high-pitched scratching sound over the left sternal border. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to reveal which of the following findings?

options.opd: Increased titer of anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Inflammatory process in the chest -> Pleuritis -> Fever, dyspnea, chest pain -> 80% CHAIN: Joint pain and stiffness -> Limited range of motion in fingers -> Difficulty working on the computer -> 70% CHAIN: High-pitched scratching sound over the left sternal border -> Pericarditis -> Chest pain worsens on deep inspiration -> 75% CHAIN: Fever, joint pain, chest pain -> Autoimmune process -> Possible autoimmune disease -> 60% CHAIN: Joint pain, limited range of motion -> Inflammatory arthritis -> 50% CHAIN: Joint pain, limited range of motion -> Rheumatoid arthritis -> Anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies -> 70% CHAIN: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies -> Rheumatoid arthritis -> Joint symptoms -> 80%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of low-grade fever, dyspnea, chest pain, joint pain, and limited range of motion in the fingers, along with the high-pitched scratching sound over the left sternal border, are suggestive of pericarditis. Given the association with joint symptoms, the most likely finding on further evaluation would be an increased titer of anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies, which are commonly seen in rheumatoid arthritis.
